subject: Vendor invoice cadence, VAT treatment, and minimum-commit carve-outs
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@cloudware.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cloudware.com, finance@cloudware.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on invoice cadence, VAT & minimum commit for Redwood Order Form

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week — CloudWare is keen to move forward but procurement has a few outstanding commercial questions before we sign the Order Form:

- Invoice cadence: can Redwood issue a single annual invoice for reserved capacity, or do you require quarterly invoicing? Our accounting prefers annual.
- Net terms: CloudWare typically does Net 45 for pilot/first-year arrangements. Is Net 45 acceptable or can we stick to Net 30?
- VAT / tax handling: CloudWare operates across EU and APAC; for our EU entity we need VAT-exclusive pricing and the ability to provide a VAT registration certificate to avoid tax collection at source.
- Minimum commits: Sales is pushing a 12-month committed spend; our FP&A is asking for a Year 1 ramp (30% of full commit) with true-up at month 9. Is that a carve-out you can accept?

I've looped in our procurement and finance teams (cc'd). If you can share a version of the Order Form with the commercial bits called out, that will speed legal review.

Regards,
Olivia Park
Sr. Procurement Manager | CloudWare
attachments: none
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@cloudware.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on invoice cadence, VAT & minimum commit for Redwood Order Form

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses below and I've attached a redline with the proposed language so legal has something concrete: RW_OrderForm_v1_stephanie_redline.pdf.

- Invoice cadence: We can accommodate annual invoicing for reserved capacity if paid upfront for the year. Otherwise our standard is quarterly invoices (invoice at start of quarter + consumption true-up at quarter-end).
- Net terms: Standard is Net 30. We can make a one-time Net 45 for the first invoice to support your cash planning; subsequent invoices would be Net 30.
- VAT: We will invoice VAT-exclusive for EU-registered entities on receipt of a valid VAT registration certificate. We'll include a tax clause that mirrors this.
- Minimum commits: We can add a Year 1 ramp to 30% of the committed amount with a true-up at month 9; will need the exact ramp schedule in the Order Form.

Next steps I propose: I will send RW_OrderForm_v1 (redline) now. If CloudWare legal returns comments, we can iterate and then get final approvals. Karthik — can you review the pricing schedule and approve the Net 45-first-invoice exception? Marissa — please confirm if the finance team needs a specific invoice layout for APAC VAT entries.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: RW_OrderForm_v1_stephanie_redline.pdf (redline PDF)
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@cloudware.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cloudware.com, CloudWare Finance <finance@cloudware.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on invoice cadence, VAT & minimum commit for Redwood Order Form

Thanks Stephanie — we reviewed the redline with legal and attached their comments: CW_OrderForm_Redlines_legal.pdf. Two points from our side:

1) Net terms: legal is pushing for Net 45 across the board for Year 1. They note our auditors prefer longer days to allow month-end cutoffs.
2) Minimum commit: they'd prefer the 30% Year 1 ramp but want a cap on overage rates during ramp (no overage charges above 120% of committed unit price for months 1–9).

Also — attached is our VAT registration for the EU entity (sent to procurement). Can Redwood include a clause that allows VAT-exclusive invoicing from execution once you have the certificate on file?

If we can get to agreement on the above this week, procurement will prepare the PO and we can sign.

Olivia Park
Sr. Procurement Manager | CloudWare
attachments: CW_OrderForm_Redlines_legal.pdf, CloudWare_EU_VAT_certificate.pdf
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@cloudware.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on invoice cadence, VAT & minimum commit for Redwood Order Form

Hi Olivia — Karthik from Commercials — appreciated the signal. We reviewed CloudWare's redlines and propose the following compromise to get this over the line quickly:

- Net terms: One-time Net 45 on the first invoice as Stephanie suggested; Net 30 thereafter. This keeps our receivable profile predictable while giving CloudWare the initial flexibility.
- Invoice cadence: Annual invoicing accepted only if the invoice is prepaid at execution. Otherwise quarterly invoices with a single annual true-up are feasible.
- VAT: Redwood will accept a valid EU VAT registration certificate on file and issue VAT-exclusive invoices going forward. We will also add an explicit representation in the Order Form requiring the buyer to notify Redwood of changes to tax status.
- Minimum commit + ramp: We can accept a Year 1 30% ramp with a true-up at month 9. Regarding your cap on overage pricing during ramp, we can commit to a cap of 110% (not 120%) of the committed unit rate for months 1–9.

I've attached a cleaned-up commercial redline (RW_OrderForm_v2_commercials.docx) with the exact phrasing for the Net term exception and the tax clause. Laura — can you review the tax clause quickly and confirm the proposed wording meets our risk tolerance?

If CloudWare is ok with 110% cap on overage pricing we can ask finance to issue the PO and Legal to finalize.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
attachments: RW_OrderForm_v2_commercials.docx (Word redline)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@cloudware.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 08:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on invoice cadence, VAT & minimum commit for Redwood Order Form

Hi Olivia — Laura from Legal. Reviewed Karthik's proposed language. The tax clause and Net terms compromise look acceptable from a legal risk perspective with two small edits:

1) Tax clause: we will accept the VAT registration certificate and invoice VAT-exclusive, but need a carve-out that Redwood is not liable for additional taxes if CloudWare's tax residency changes mid-term. Suggested sentence added to the clause.
2) Minimum commit true-up: we require the true-up calculation to be explicit in the Order Form (months, metric used, rounding rules). I added a one-line formula so there is no ambiguity.

I've attached the short redline for the tax sentence and true-up formula: TaxClause_Redline.txt. If CloudWare confirms the VAT certificate and accepts the 110% overage cap, we can have the final Order Form executed today and finance can proceed with the PO. Also provided a DocuSign link for expedited signature in the redline.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
attachments: TaxClause_Redline.txt, DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABCDEF1234567890
